items.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021
items.q: Danny would have a private session with me. There was no standard price. Every load of records was his own negotiation.

ctx.x: Okay. So you started re-issuing these Sun Ra records while Sun Ra was still alive.

Of course. By the way as far as Danny Thompson goes I’d like to tell one more anecdote. When he would bring records into the store, sometimes, you know, Sun Ra would come along with him you know, in the Cadillac. And that’s why Sun Ra, you know, came into the store, and let’s go down to Third Street, and Sun Ra would look around and then Danny would have a private session with me. There was no standard price. Every load of records was his own negotiation. I had to do it over and over again every time I saw them.…

I’ve got to ask you, Sun Ra is well known for having had certain moral standards and standards of behavior and not liking drugs and alcohol, things like that. And I can think of one Sun Ra record where there’s a very prominent profanity in the song “Nuclear War.”
